title: ～させられる — causative-passive (“be made to ～”)
summary: It combines the causative (させる) and the passive (られる): “to be made to do ～ by someone”. The person who is forced is the subject, and there is usually a feeling of reluctance.

patterns.gloss: Group 1: ない-stem + される (読む → 読まされる)
Group 2: stem + させられる (食べる → 食べさせられる)
Group 3: する → させられる, 来る → 来させられる

body.p: 母にピアノを練習させられた means “Mother made me practice (causative) and I had to go through it (passive).” It usually carries a feeling of “I didn’t want to, but had to”.
For group 1 verbs the shorter form is normal: 読まされる rather than 読ませられる (but 話す → 話させられる). The person who forces you is marked with に, and the action with を.

examples.ja: 子（こ）どもの時（とき）、毎日（まいにち）ピアノを練習（れんしゅう）させられました。
examples.romaji: Kodomo no toki, mainichi piano o renshū saseraremashita.
examples.tr: As a child, I was made to practice piano every day.

examples.ja: 上司（じょうし）に急（きゅう）な仕事（しごと）をさせられた。
examples.romaji: Jōshi ni kyū na shigoto o saserareta.
examples.tr: I was made to do a sudden task by my boss.

examples.ja: 弟（おとうと）は毎日（まいにち）野菜（やさい）を食（た）べさせられている。
examples.romaji: Otōto wa mainichi yasai o tabesaserarete iru.
examples.tr: My little brother is made to eat vegetables every day.

pitfalls: The person being forced is the subject, not the person who forces.
Group 1 verbs usually use the short form (読まされる), except 話す → 話させられる.
